greek: Καὶ ηὐλόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν Νωε καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε καὶ πληρώσατε τὴν γῆν καὶ κατακυριεύσατε αὐτῆς.
hint: God blesses Noah and his sons with the words of 1:28.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *pĕrû ûrĕbû ûmilʾû ʾet-hāʾāreṣ*, *be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth*, and stops. The Greek adds *and gain dominion over it*, the last command of 1:28.
The first sense in the passive, as at 8:17: αὐξάνω *to make large*, πληθύνω *to make full*; the passives' own *to grow* and *to prevail* stand last in the chains.
κατακυριεύω has one sense in Middle Liddell, *to gain dominion over*, so it is plain text.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ὁ τρόμος ὑμῶν καὶ ὁ φόβος ἔσται ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς θηρίοις τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ κινούμενα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἰχθύας τῆς θαλάσσης· ὑπὸ χεῖρας ὑμῖν δέδωκα.
hint: The fear of man falls on every creature, given under his hands.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *môraʾăkem wĕḥittĕkem*, *the fear of you and the dread of you*. τρόμος is *a trembling, quaking*; φόβος is first *flight*, its only sense in Homer, and *fear* after it.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕyedkem nittānû*, *into your hand they are given*, passive. The Greek has God speak, *under hands to you I have given*, in the perfect: a gift that stands.
ὑπό with the accusative: Middle Liddell's first sense for that case is *towards and under*, motion that ends beneath. The phrase is the idiom *into your power*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out the last ἐπί.

hint: Only flesh with its blood is withheld.

greek: ὁ ἐκχέων αἷμα ἀνθρώπου ἀντὶ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ ἐκχυθήσεται, ὅτι ἐν εἰκόνι θεοῦ ἐποίησα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
hint: Blood for blood, because man was made in God's likeness.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *šōpēk dam hāʾādām bāʾādām dāmô yiššāpēk*, *whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed*. The Greek has no *by man*: *the one pouring out blood of a man, over against his blood, will be poured out*.
[[flag]] *I made*: the Hebrew is *ʿāśâ*, *he made*, of God in the third person.
The Hebrew *bĕṣelem ʾĕlōhîm*, the phrase of 1:27, where the Greek had κατʼ εἰκόνα θεοῦ.
ἐκχέω, *to pour out*, in the future passive; the entry's own senses for the passive, from *to stream out* to *to lie languidly*, stand last.
Middle Liddell gives ἀντί first as *over against, opposite*, then *instead of*, *at the price of, for*. Perseus's summary and the senses for compounds are left out.

greek: ἐξένηψεν δὲ Νωε ἀπὸ τοῦ οἴνου καὶ ἔγνω ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ νεώτερος,
hint: Noah becomes sober and learns what his younger son did.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyîqeṣ*, *and he awoke*. The Greek has ἐκνήφω, *to sleep off a drunken fit, become sober again*.
The comparative of νέος, *young*: *the younger*, for the Hebrew *haqqāṭān*, *the small, the youngest*.

reading: [[slept off a drunken fit|slept off a drunken fit / became sober again|ἐκνήφω]] [[but|but, however, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Νωε]] [[from|from, away from, away from / far from / apart from, alien from, of, from / after, sprung from, in descent from, born of, from or of, from or by, because of, by reason of, moved by / for, what is one's own|ἀπό]] of the wine and [[learned to know|learned to know / perceived / marked / learned, discerned / distinguished, thou mayst discern, were aware of, I felt that I was, that he may learn how to, observed / formed a judgment on, judged / thought, I understand, judged / determined / decreed that|γινώσκω]] [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] [[made|made, did, made / produced / created, composed / wrote, made / represented in poetry, described in verse, put into verse, brought to pass / brought about / caused, held, acted, worked / operated|ποιέω]] to him the son of him [[the younger|the younger / more youthful, the more suited to a youth / more youthful, the newer / fresher, the newer / more strange, the stranger|νέος]],

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ἐπικατάρατος Χανααν· παῖς οἰκέτης ἔσται τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.
hint: The curse falls on Canaan.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿebed ʿăbādîm*, *a servant of servants*. The Greek has two nouns side by side, *a child, a house-slave*.
Middle Liddell's first sense is *a child*, in relation to descent; *a slave, servant* is its third, in relation to condition.
*Yet more accursed*, the one sense of 3:14, plain text.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said / spoke, said / declared, said something of, called by name, told, boasted of / told of, recited|λέγω]] yet more accursed [[name:Χανααν]]; [[a child|a child, a son / daughter, a boy / youth / lad, a girl / maiden, a slave / servant / man / maid|παῖς]] [[a house-slave|a house-slave / menial|οἰκέτης]] will be [[to the sons of the same mother|to the sons of the same mother, to the brothers, to the near kinsmen, to the brother and sisters|ἀδελφός]] of him.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Σημ, καὶ ἔσται Χανααν παῖς αὐτοῦ.
hint: Noah calls the Lord God of Shem blessed: the words that open the Benedictus.

notes.lemma: Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Σημ
notes.text: The Hebrew *bārûk YHWH ʾĕlōhê šēm*. The same words open Zechariah's song in Luke 1:68, Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ. εὐλογητός has one sense, *blessed*, and is plain text.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *wîhî*, *and let … be*, a wish. The Greek has the future, *will be*, and *of him* for the Hebrew *lāmô*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said / spoke, said / declared, said something of, called by name, told, boasted of / told of, recited|λέγω]] blessed [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of the [[name:Σημ]], and will be [[name:Χανααν]] [[a child|a child, a son / daughter, a boy / youth / lad, a girl / maiden, a slave / servant / man / maid|παῖς]] of him.

greek: πλατύναι ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ιαφεθ καὶ κατοικησάτω ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις τοῦ Σημ, καὶ γενηθήτω Χανααν παῖς αὐτῶν.
hint: Noah wishes God to widen Japheth; the Hebrew play between the verb and the name is lost.

notes.text: The aorist optative, a wish. The Hebrew *yapt ʾĕlōhîm lĕyepet* plays the verb *pātâ*, *to make wide*, against the name *Yepet*; πλατύνω, *to widen*, keeps the sense and loses the play.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾohŏlê-šēm*, *in the tents of Shem*. The Greek has *houses*, as at 9:21.
κατοικέω's first translation, *to dwell in as a κάτοικος*, leaves its last word in Greek; the headword stops at *dwell in*.

reading: [[may widen|may widen / make wide|πλατύνω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] to the [[name:Ιαφεθ]] and [[let him dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|let him dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), let him settle in / colonise, let him inhabit, let him settle / dwell, let him lie / be situate|κατοικέω]] [[in the houses|within, inside of, and by means of the houses / abodes / dwellings, the homes / withins, the parts of a house / rooms / chambers, the single houses, the houses of a god / temples, the one's houses / household goods / substances, the houses / households / families|ἐν; οἶκος]] of the [[name:Σημ]], and [[let come into being|let come to be, let arise, let be brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[name:Χανααν]] [[a child|a child, a son / daughter, a boy / youth / lad, a girl / maiden, a slave / servant / man / maid|παῖς]] of them.

greek: Ἔζησεν δὲ Νωε μετὰ τὸν κατακλυσμὸν τριακόσια πεντήκοντα ἔτη.
hint: Noah lives three hundred and fifty years after the flood.

notes.text: The Hebrew *šĕlōš mēʾôt šānâ waḥămiššîm šānâ*; the numbers agree.

reading: [[lived|lived, lived off or on, was in full life / strength / fresh and strong|ζάω]] [[but|but, however, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Νωε]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit / quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[the deluge|the deluge / inundation|κατακλυσμός]] three hundred fifty years.

greek: καὶ ἐγένοντο πᾶσαι αἱ ἡμέραι Νωε ἐννακόσια πεντήκοντα ἔτη, καὶ ἀπέθανεν.
hint: Noah dies at nine hundred and fifty.

notes.text: The frame of chapter 5, closing the last life of that genealogy.
